A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the deformation and damage accumulation properties of solder alloys under realistic service conditions are more complex than is generally assumed.
the effects of thermal cycling on the deformation and damage properties of the solder are not well understood, and the effects on solder joint reliability are not well characterized.
the reliability of microelectronics solder joints in realistic environments is not adequately addressed by current accelerated testing protocols.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the effects of thermal cycling on the mechanical properties of solder joints are not fully accounted for by accelerated testing with fixed amplitude, and that the acceleration factor is dependent on the thermal cycling history.
accelerated testing for solder joint reliability must be conducted with a range of amplitudes to avoid underestimating the ultimate service life of the component.

accelerated testing of microelectronics components is a complex problem, and that a single test method is unlikely to be able to provide the necessary information for reliable predictions of service life.
